summary.headline: Jindal Stainless Q1 FY27: revenue up 10.5% YoY and PAT up 7.7%, but finished-goods volume fell 7.3% on gas shortages; FY27 volume guidance held.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was resilient on profit but weak on volume, as industrial gas (LPG/propane) shortages and Middle East logistics issues hit the first weeks of April 2026. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 10.5%, 1.4% and 7.7% YoY, with management prioritising value-added mix and thinner grades. Consolidated net debt fell to INR 2,950 crore (net debt/EBITDA 0.53x). Management kept FY27 volume guidance (8-10% growth) and the INR 18,000-20,000/t H1 EBITDA guidance, deferring any revision to the next quarter. Indonesia melt shop (1.2 MTPA) has started ramping up; the Jindal Stainless Indonesia structure changed from subsidiary to associate effective 1 July 2026.

segments.name: Chromeni (Indonesia / subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 80-85%; described as the major contributor in Q1 because it ran fully on pipe natural gas during the disruption.

segments.name: Rathi Steel (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Utilisation about 70% (Q1 hit by fuel shortage; about 80% before disruption); product mix being optimised each quarter.

segments.name: Rabirun (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: EBITDA positive but small polishing business; cold rolling and BA line investment to be operational in FY28.

segments.name: Indonesia 1.2 MTPA melt shop (PTGMI)
segments.commentary: Recently commissioned; ramping up after local approvals and certifications, with sales expected to build gradually. Now an associate from 1 July 2026.

segments.name: RKEF / nickel business
segments.commentary: EBITDA positive in the last two quarters and in Q1 per management; volatile, mainly a raw material security play.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume growth of 8-10% held; management to update in Q2 (end of next quarter) and expects only gradual recovery in volume over the next few quarters.
H1 FY27 EBITDA per tonne guidance of INR 18,000-20,000 maintained; no revision yet.
FY27 capex plan of INR 2,400-2,600 crore is on track; cold rolling capacity to rise from 2 MTPA to at least 2.67 MTPA by FY28.
Target sales volume of 3.5 MTPA by FY29 reaffirmed.
HRAP (1.1 MTPA first phase) expected to be ready around end of Q3 FY27.
Indonesia ramp-up targeted at 70-80% utilisation in the first year of operation, per partner's track record.
Jajpur green hydrogen: 600 Nm3/hr expected to commission in August 2026; another 600 Nm3/hr planned next year; Hisar 200 Nm3/hr over next two quarters.
Maharashtra greenfield plant: detailed plan deferred by another one to two quarters pending land acquisition.
capex_capacity: Downstream projects at Jajpur, Hisar and Kharagpur progressing; new equipment coming up each quarter over the next year, starting with Jajpur, then Kharagpur, then Hisar.
HRAP (1.1 MTPA first phase) expected around end of Q3 FY27, versus earlier expectation of first half FY27.
Cold rolling capacity target of at least 2.67 MTPA by FY28, up from 2 MTPA.
Pipe natural gas introduced at Jajpur; similar plans for Hisar and Ghaziabad.
Hisar greenhouse gas emission intensity down 12% YoY from energy-efficient ancillaries and waste heat recovery.
demand_pricing: Management says demand was never the issue in Q1; the shortfall came from gas and logistics constraints, and whatever is produced will be sold.
Sales grew in automotive, appliances, white goods, railways and metro; Vande Bharat ferritic-to-austenitic shift and K-RIDE (ICF Chennai) spec support value-added grades.

Export volumes flat QoQ in absolute terms; export share rose only because the base shrank. Europe is roughly 30-40% of exports, and Europe plus US about 60%. Management targets new markets (Japan, South Korea, Brazil, Colombia) only where margins are good.
Pricing: gas cost pass-through to customers works in both directions, with a lag; the company could not pass on the full gas cost increase in Q1.
Scrap feed: Hisar about 85-90%, Jajpur about 70-75% (general); 90-95% of scrap sourced from domestic and Southeast Asia, less than 2-3% from Europe.
Antidumping duty: DGTR public hearing scheduled 9 September 2026; verifiers being appointed. QCO extended to March 2027, with management expecting no reversal before then.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management on 8-10% FY27 volume growth, and are exports (about 11% of volume) sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance held for H1 with a fresh view in H2 if needed. Export volumes were stable QoQ; the higher share reflects a lower base, and the company intends to maintain export volumes to support EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Did the gas shortage cost volume, and could margins have been better without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 volume guidance would otherwise have been met and that margins were better in principle; not all of the gas price increase could be passed on because India's cost rise was steeper than competitors'.

qa_highlights.question: Has production returned to pre-war levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Shift from propane/LPG to pipe natural gas at Jajpur eased supply and cost pressure, and management says production is back to pre-disruption levels.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 grade mix and power and fuel trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix was 35% 200-series, 47% 300-series, 18% 400-series. Power and fuel fell 40-50% from the Q1 peak, but has not returned to pre-war levels and fluctuates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Maharashtra greenfield project and the Indonesia ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra still in land acquisition; detailed plan in another one to two quarters. Indonesia is ramping up, with 70-80% first-year utilisation expected; no further Indonesia capacity planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PTGMI move from subsidiary to associate?
qa_highlights.answer: Control was held during construction; now in operation, the partner runs it, so JSL gave up board majority effective 1 July 2026. Share of profit will be booked as associate income; slab supply contract rights are unchanged and guidance is not affected.

risks_watch: Volume recovery is gradual; June-July volumes not disclosed. Management will update in Q2.
Energy cost volatility: gas and LPG prices are still fluctuating, and pass-through lags.
Export pressure: EU quota reduction and Middle East war reduce EU and MENA volumes; new-market volumes take several quarters.
Regulatory: antidumping public hearing on 9 September 2026; QCO extension to March 2027 with risk of further extension.
Nickel/RKEF business volatility from Indonesian nickel ore policy changes.
Maharashtra greenfield project still lacks land and a firm plan.
Working capital and closing inventory (tonnage) not disclosed; management to follow up.
Indonesia melt shop ramp-up pace and the associate accounting change.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and balance sheet, but cautious and deferential on volume and margin guidance, which is being held until next quarter. Management was evasive on specifics (June-July volumes, CBAM intensity, inventory, PTGMI blast furnace), and repeatedly deferred numbers to later updates.

growth.why: FY27 sales volume growth of 8-10% held (midpoint 9%), backed by HRAP 1.1 MTPA due around end Q3 FY27, Indonesia melt shop ramp-up and cold rolling expansion to 2.67 MTPA by FY28, but Q1 finished-goods volume fell 7.3% YoY and utilisation is only ~70%, so the guidance rests on partial rather than fully contracted evidence.
